background: Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) is one of the three note-issuing banks in Hong Kong and the largest subsidiary of Standard Chartered, funded by Hong Kong deposits and lending to corporates, households and across the group's Asian network.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, A+ on average, both on a stable outlook. Capital and liquidity are strong against Asian banks, with CET1 of 16.9%, leverage of 6.4% and LCR of 170% in the top quarter and NSFR of 128% above the peer median. The direction is downward, though from a high base: since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has fallen 2.1 points, LCR 35 points and NSFR 12 points, in figures to 30 Jun 2026.
